originalTitle: Website behind widely shared fake election polls run by 21-year-old
summary: Exclusive: Rahil Prakash tells the Guardian: ‘I wanted to see if fake polls could penetrate the ecosystem that easily’
content: A 21-year-old recent college graduate was behind an anonymous website that put out widely shared fake election polling in Wisconsin, Nevada and California, the Guardian can reveal. The website, Median Strategies, abruptly shut down and withdrew its polling earlier this week following questions from a reporter from the Los Angeles Times. In an unsigned statement, it described a “short-term social experiment” to examine how fake polling “could enter and spread through the political information ecosystem without independent verification”. “I wanted to see if fake polls could really penetrate the ecosystem that easily,” Rahil Prakash told the Guardian on Thursday when reached by phone. “And as it turned out, it could.” Karen Bass, the mayor of Los Angeles, touted Median polling data after it appeared to put her ahead of her election challenger by more than 10 percentage points. The poll was also cited by the California Post. A widely followed polling aggregator on X also shared the group’s Nevada poll, although several credible polling organizations did not aggregate Median polling because they could not verify its methodology. “Did I expect it to perhaps expedite in the way it did? Most definitely not,” said Prakash. “I did not expect the California political press to pick it up on their own.” He added: “I’ll apologize straight out to the campaigns of Karen Bass, Nithya Raman and Francesca Hong for this.” Raman is running against Bass in November’s LA mayoral election. Hong lost the Democratic primary for Wisconsin governor earlier this month, after Median suggested she had led the race by more than 20 percentage points. It also released a fake poll showing the Nevada governor, Joe Lombardo, up by five points before November’s general election. In an interview, Prakash said he was motivated to start the fake polling project after a significant polling miss in the Michigan Senate primary, where polls had showed Abdul El-Sayed with a heavy lead over his opponent Haley Stevens before election day. In the event, El-Sayed wound up winning by a much smaller margin than polls had suggested. “This is what inspired me to test my theory,” said Prakash. “I was a bit shocked, perhaps at how fast this sort of information can spread.” As of Thursday morning, Median had about 20 followers on its X account. According to the Los Angeles Times, the account began posting on 9 August. “I think my overall takeaway was that if you just make it look a bit pretty, it’s rather easy for it to spread,” Prakash said. “And I hope it gives a really good lesson going forward in that we need to be very serious about these things and very serious in how, if one person can do this, what can a serious operation do in the future – a real, you know, operation for an organization, country, whatever.” Prakash, who said that he made the website using artificial intelligence, said he alone created Median. The Guardian identified Prakash using domain registration data tied to the Median Strategies website. By reverse-searching two domain nameservers tied to the site, the Guardian obtained lists of several thousand other domains also using those nameservers. About 115 domains used the same two nameservers, but only one used the same two nameservers and used the same domain name registrar as Median Strategies. Only a GitHub 404 message appears on that matching website now. But additional web records tied it to a GitHub profile, which included a file with Prakash’s name. The lengthy anonymous statement on Monday posted to Median’s website also stressed that “no individual involved with Median Strategies received compensation or financial benefit from the project”, which it claimed had not been “funded, commissioned or directed” by any campaign, party, media outlet or other “outside entity”. When asked on Thursday whether he had traded on any prediction markets after publishing the sham data, Prakash said: “No, not at all.” On Wednesday, before the Guardian contacted Prakash, the American Association of Political Consultants condemned the effort. “Publishing fabricated survey data as independent research is not a social experiment,” it said, describing the project as “a deception directed at voters, at the press, and at the campaigns that rely on public data to make decisions”. Aaron Zolla contributed with digital forensics
chineseTitle: 21 岁男子发起的虚假选举民意调查被广泛传播
chineseSummary: 独家：拉希尔·普拉卡什 (Rahil Prakash) 告诉《卫报》：“我想看看虚假民意调查是否可以轻易渗透到生态系统中”
chineseContent: 据《卫报》透露，一名 21 岁的应届大学毕业生是一个匿名网站的幕后黑手，该网站在威斯康星州、内华达州和加利福尼亚州发布了广泛传播的虚假选举民意调查。本周早些时候，在接受《洛杉矶时报》记者的提问后，该网站“中位数策略”突然关闭并撤回了民意调查。在一份未签署的声明中，它描述了一项“短期社会实验”，以研究虚假民意调查“如何在未经独立验证的情况下进入并通过政治信息生态系统传播”。周四，拉希尔·普拉卡什 (Rahil Prakash) 在电话中告诉《卫报》：“我想看看虚假民意调查是否真的能那么容易地渗透到生态系统中。” “事实证明，它可以。”洛杉矶市长凯伦·巴斯 (Karen Bass) 对中位民意调查数据大肆吹捧，因为该数据似乎让她领先竞选挑战者 10 个百分点以上。 《加州邮报》也引用了这项民意调查。 X 上广受关注的民意调查聚合商也分享了该组织的内华达州民意调查，尽管一些可信的民意调查组织没有汇总中位数民意调查，因为他们无法验证其方法。 “我是否期望它会像以前那样加速？绝对不是，”普拉卡什说。 “我没想到加州的政治媒体会自己发现这件事。”他补充道：“我将为此直接向凯伦·巴斯、尼西亚·拉曼和弗朗西斯卡·洪的竞选团队道歉。”拉曼将在 11 月的洛杉矶市长选举中与巴斯竞选。本月早些时候，洪在威斯康星州州长的民主党初选中落败，此前梅迪恩表示她在竞选中领先 20 个百分点以上。它还发布了一份虚假民意调查，显示内华达州州长乔·隆巴多 (Joe Lombardo) 在 11 月大选前的支持率上升了 5 个百分点。普拉卡什在接受采访时表示
